description: Authoritative development corpus with traceable official U.S. sources spanning medication interactions, renal/hepatic impairment, allergy, pregnancy, age-specific hypoglycemia, QT/electrolyte risk, immunosuppression/infection, asthma/NSAID risk, sepsis, and stroke red flags. Not primary_frozen until benchmark coverage and expert review are complete.

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for warfarin sodium
records.title: Warfarin sodium — drugs that increase bleeding risk
records.excerpt: The warfarin label identifies nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, including ibuprofen and naproxen, among concomitant medicines that increase bleeding risk and calls for close monitoring when used together.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed
records.source_locator: Section 7.3, Drugs that Increase Bleeding Risk

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for ibuprofen tablets
records.title: Ibuprofen — renal effects and advanced renal disease
records.excerpt: Ibuprofen labeling identifies impaired renal function as a risk factor for NSAID-related renal decompensation and states that treatment is not recommended in advanced renal disease unless benefits justify use with renal monitoring.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for amoxicillin
records.title: Amoxicillin — serious beta-lactam hypersensitivity contraindication
records.excerpt: Amoxicillin is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions to amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs, including penicillins and cephalosporins.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.title: NSAID use in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later
records.excerpt: FDA warns that NSAID use around 20 weeks of pregnancy or later can cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios; prescribing should generally be limited between 20 and 30 weeks and avoided after about 30 weeks, with the stated low-dose aspirin exception.
records.source_locator: Additional Information for Health Care Professionals

records.title: Sepsis — life-threatening emergency and warning signs
records.excerpt: CDC describes sepsis as a life-threatening medical emergency and lists warning features including confusion or disorientation, extreme pain or discomfort, fever or feeling very cold, high heart rate or weak pulse, clammy skin, and shortness of breath.
records.source_org: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
records.source_locator: About Sepsis — Key points and Signs and symptoms

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for metformin hydrochloride
records.title: Metformin — renal impairment thresholds
records.excerpt: Metformin labeling contraindicates use when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², discourages initiation when eGFR is 30–45, and requires reassessment or discontinuation as renal function declines.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed
records.source_locator: Section 2.3, Recommendations for Use in Renal Impairment

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for ibuprofen tablets
records.title: Ibuprofen — aspirin-sensitive asthma and NSAID cross-reactivity
records.excerpt: Ibuprofen labeling states that patients with asthma or allergic-type reactions after aspirin or other NSAIDs should not receive ibuprofen, and warns about severe bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.source: DailyMed U.S. prescribing information for acetaminophen injection
records.title: Acetaminophen — severe hepatic impairment / active liver disease
records.excerpt: Acetaminophen labeling states that use is contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment or severe active liver disease and advises caution/reduced total daily dosing in hepatic impairment.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for citalopram tablets
records.title: Citalopram — QT prolongation and electrolyte risk
records.version_or_date: DailyMed label updated 2025-08-04; QT warning section 5.2
records.excerpt: Citalopram labeling warns of dose-dependent QTc prolongation and advises avoidance in patients with hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia and in those taking other QT-prolonging drugs; electrolyte monitoring is advised in patients at risk.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed
records.source_locator: Section 5.2, QT-Prolongation and Torsade de Pointes

records.source: DailyMed U.S. prescribing information for glyburide tablets
records.title: Glyburide — older adults and severe hypoglycemia risk
records.excerpt: Glyburide labeling states that older adults are particularly susceptible to hypoglycemia, which may be difficult to recognize, and recommends conservative dosing with attention to renal function.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.source: DailyMed current U.S. prescribing information for methotrexate tablets
records.title: Methotrexate — serious and opportunistic infection risk
records.excerpt: Methotrexate labeling states that treated patients are at increased risk for life-threatening or fatal bacterial, fungal, or viral infections, including opportunistic infections, and recommends monitoring and withholding or discontinuing therapy for serious infection as appropriate.
records.source_org: U.S. National Library of Medicine / DailyMed

records.title: Stroke — sudden neurologic warning signs and emergency response
records.excerpt: CDC lists sudden unilateral numbness or weakness, confusion or speech difficulty, vision trouble, gait/balance problems, and sudden severe headache as stroke warning signs and advises calling emergency services immediately.
records.source_org: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
records.source_locator: Signs and symptoms; When to seek emergency help
